h: Zoos, Roman chariots and Constable Country
p: Colchester likes to call itself Britain's oldest recorded town, and history is everywhere you turn. One fascinating spot is the remains of a Roman chariot-racing circus, uncovered in the 2000s on the south side of the town. Another is the Jumbo water tower, a huge Victorian landmark visible across the town. Once you've finished bouncing, a stroll around the old streets and the castle is a lovely way to cool down.

Colchester Zoo, out at Stanway on the western edge of the town, is one of the region's big family days out, with elephants, big cats, giraffes and much more. It's easy to pair with an AirHop session if you're staying a couple of days. Firstsite, the contemporary art gallery near the town centre, is free and often has family activities.

For a change of scene, Mersea Island is a short drive away, famous for its oysters, beach huts and wide views over the estuary. Just be aware that the causeway, the Strood, can flood at very high tides. To the north, Dedham Vale is Constable Country, where the painter John Constable grew up, and the walk between Dedham and Flatford along the River Stour is a gentle, beautiful stroll. A tip for AirHop: the AR trampolines and reaction walls can draw a crowd, so try them early in your session. Bring a water bottle for every jumper, as the games are properly energetic. Colchester is easy to reach from much of Essex and Suffolk, so a bounce slots neatly into a day trip, and the town's mainline station has trains to London. If you've time to spare, the walk through Castle Park down to the River Colne is a lovely, relaxed way to round things off.
